corrections: Dedicated clean F/A18C shell, tapered radome, true single canopy aperture, curved LEX joined continuously to fuselage, paired round-sided intakes and F404 fairings, thin swept wings, canted fins and stabilators.

Used NATOPS clean37ft6in span rather than missile-inclusive40ft5in span. Preserved56ft length,15ft3in fin height,10ft6in canopy and20degree fin cant; NASA baseline three-view supplies contours without research booms.

Corrected LEX gaps revealed by top overlay, console walls protruding into exterior, attitude mask protruding above coaming, floating fasteners and retracted gear intersecting cabin. Gear is hidden when fully retracted behind the closed bay.

Late-C FO5 layout: two upper DDIs, central UFC keypad and five option fields, lower MPCD, left IFEI and right standby cluster. Physical HUD/coaming, SJU17-inspired seat/harness, center stick, pedals and twin left throttles.

Live attitude, TAS, geometric altitude including signed display, vertical speed and true heading. DDI and MPCD presentations are simplified simulator displays; unmodeled radar/engine/fuel/hydraulic/clock quantities blank or INOP.

Animated leading flaps, trailing flaps, ailerons, differential stabilators, rudders, gear and pilot controls through shared named expressions. Independent imported-node tests cover calibration, control directions, cardinal headings, missing readings and gear-bay visibility.
Canopy rail/bow fasteners, selected access seams, wing fastener rows, tail fairings and warning stencils are geometry; no photo textures or external weapons.
independentDimensions: NATOPS56ft=17.0688m length;37ft6in=11.43m clean span;15ft3in=4.6482m fin height;10ft6in=3.2004m canopy height. Rail/fin thickness extends measured runtime bounds slightly to11.4398m span,4.6601m height.
NASA21.6ft=6.58368m stabilator span and400ft2=37.161216m2 nominal aerodynamic wing area. Main track2.96m and wheelbase5.38m reconstructed from the drawing, not independent manufacturing dimensions.

Uniform length scale for side/top; rear-elevation width calibrated independently to NASA37.4ft. Rear elevation differs vertically from stated canopy/fin dimensions and side view by roughly10percent. Kept actual NATOPS dimensions and disclosed discrepancy; no stretched axes.

Panel normalized from FO5, nominal5in DDI screen used as scale. Panel/seat depth and installation are reconstructed from photos. Swiss airshow cockpit photo checks depth and housings only; national avionics differences do not override US late-C foldout.
reviewNotes.visual: Inspected four overlays, eight standard views and ten detail/instrument states. Rechecked all22 current-geometry captures in six contact sheets, plus full-size seated cruise after correcting gear intrusion. Compared actual US Navy exterior and canopy/HUD photos, public-domain cockpit photo and both FO5 panel/console foldouts.
limitations: Polygonal interpretation, not an engineering replica. Airfoil sections, compound fuselage curvature, inlet ducts, canopy refraction, individual fastener positions, stencils and unit livery remain simplified. NASA drawings have disclosed scale disagreements.
Panel main instrument positions follow the foldout; switch counts, console spacing, dial marks, seat and harness details remain approximations. Static switches do not operate aircraft systems.

DDI attitude/TAS/geometric-altitude and MPCD true-heading are simplified simulator presentations, not authentic Hornet software pages. No collimated HUD, radar/RWR, navigation map, flight director, magnetic heading, calibrated IAS/Mach or pressure altitude.
IFEI core RPM,temperature,fuel flow,nozzle schedule,fuel quantity/time,hydraulic and cabin pressure are unsupported and unavailable. No fabricated power-to-engine-readout conversion.

Shared simplified flight physics and visual control mixes, not Hornet flight-control laws or automatic flap schedules. Gear retraction is an approximate animation with closed-bay hiding; no mechanical linkage/bay simulation, wing-fold control, launch-bar or carrier arresting operation.
Reference imagery/PDFs are local study material only. Source URLs and license information retained; no reference pixels redistributed in model textures.

proportionReview.outcome: Exterior reworked from measured tables; side and plan overlays and a photo match inspected.
proportionReview.method: Drawing resampled into model metres from two control points and overlaid on the rasterized GLB; dark-pixel runs per row and column turned outlines into numbers. Photographs solved as a pinhole camera with nose and canopy held out of the fit, then the imported model rendered through that camera and blended with the photograph.

calibration.side: NASA TM-4786 figure 2 (CCITT scan, 300 dpi) at 84.4 px/m: 56 ft bar, 5.38 m wheelbase and 10.5 ft canopy bar all agree. Its drawn fin is 89 px/m against the 15.3 ft bar, 5 percent tall.
calibration.plan: Nose to tail 84.4 px/m after rotating 0.5 degrees to the drawn centerline. Drawn stabilator span is 4 percent short of its 21.6 ft bar.
calibration.rear: Not to the same scale as the side view (fin measures 4.14 m). No heights taken from it.
calibration.photo: Three wheel contacts plus four fin-tip corners. Solved with the annotated 4.648 m fin: 172 m, 3.1 degrees, 8.4 px. Solved with a 4.80 m fin, the value wheelbase scale gives: same geometry, 10.2 px, but range drifts to 498 m because the view is nearly orthographic, so that camera distance is not meaningful.

landmarks.crownNasaMinusPhoto: A near constant 0.14 to 0.20 m from z 10.1 to z 1.6, which is why the side-view outline was trusted for shape.

corrections: The thin-forebody look came from the LEX, not the nose. It sat near the canopy rail and cut the fuselage side; it now runs well down the flank, leaving the tall body side the photographs show.
Spine raised, rail raised so the glass is shallower, rear body and tail fairings lifted and narrowed behind the wing, nozzles respaced with a slight axis droop.
Station-table fuselage with rail rings, wing root lowered and thickened, fin tip chord lengthened with a fixed tip overhanging a rudder on a tilted hinge, fin roots run into the narrower fairing.
Track, tire sizes, nose bay doors and arresting hook set to the drawing and photographs.
limitations: Fin height disagrees. Annotated 15 ft 3 in with 10 ft 6 in canopy gives a ratio of 1.45; the NASA drawing and the photograph both give 1.51, about 0.15 m taller at the fin. The annotated NATOPS height is kept, so the fins sit 0.15 m below the photograph when the body is matched.
NASA drawing and photograph differ on body depth by up to 0.1 m forward of the windscreen. The drawing was used; the LEX height is weighted toward the photograph.
Swiss photograph was not solved, and Commons rate-limited further requests, so no camera ahead of the beam confirms the nose.
proportionReview.note: instrumentReview captures predate this exterior rework; cockpit instruments, eye points and controls were not moved, only the tub liner rises to the new rail. Targeted aircraft tests were rerun.

cockpitSweep.finding: The seat stood about 0.8 m behind the eye. The seatback ray read nothing because it passed through the gap below the headbox. The combiner was 0.08 m tall and wholly below the horizon line, so the seat view showed no HUD.
changes: Seat forward 0.41 m and up 0.19 m; stick forward 0.20 m and 0.20 m taller; pedals aft 0.27 m and up 0.02 m; consoles and throttles up 0.10 m.
Combiner top raised from 2.78 to 3.02 m: it is now visible from the seat with the horizon through it.
Bulkhead behind the seat and an avionics deck close the well the seat left.
limitations: Seat, stick, pedal and throttle positions come from seated-eye ergonomic targets and cockpit photographs, not a dimensioned installation drawing.
The combiner is plain glass with no symbology. The deck behind the seat is a plain reconstruction.
